The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:

The Iatan Generating Station is located North of the city of Weston, Missouri at 20250 State Route 45 N.  The facility is situated east of the Missouri River.  The property is in a river valley with large hills to the South and East.

Anhydrous ammonia is used at the Iatan Generating Station as an air pollution control additive, to reduce the nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions to the atmosphere from the unit boilers. Each boiler unit is equipped with a selective catalytic reduction (SCR) device. The station is a non-responding facility for releases of the RMP-listed chemicals, so the site utilizes an Emergency Action Plan.

The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:

The ammonia storage tanks are designed to be filled by a tanker truck at a dedicated loading station.  For the Nox control systems, ammonia vapors will be drawn from the tanks, regulated for pressure, mixed with air, and injected into the boiler flue within the ammonia injection grid.  In combination with the catalyst in the selective catalytic reduction units, nitrogen oxides will be reacted and emissions of the pollutant will be reduced.

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:

Evergy has a program in place to comply with the provisions of the accidental release prevention regulations under 40 CFR Part 68. The following sections briefly describe the elements of the existing release prevention program.

Process Safety Information [40 CFR Part 68.65]
Evergy Iatan maintains a record of process safety information that describes the chemical hazards, operating parameters and equipment designs associated with the ammonia processes.

Process Hazard Analysis [40 CFR Part 68.67]
Process hazard analyses were performed using 'What If/Checklist' methodology for the Unit #1 and #2 ammonia system.  During the

PHAs, each system was methodically assessed and evaluated. Points in the system where ammonia could potentially be released were identified.  Comments and recommendations are summarized in the Process Hazard Analysis section of the Risk Management Program and are resolved in a timely manner.

Operating Procedures [40 CFR Part 68.69]
To ensure safe operations, Evergy maintains detailed written operating procedures. Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for startup, shutdown, normal operation and emergency operation of both ammonia storage systems are in place. The SOPs are posted in appropriate areas. The information is regularly reviewed and is readily accessible to operators involved in the process.

Training [40 CFR Part 68.71]
Personnel are trained annually on safety concerns and general operation procedures as well as emergency procedures. Refresher training is provided at least every three years and more frequently as needed.

Mechanical Integrity [40 CFR Part 68.73]
The ammonia systems are visually inspected on a regular basis. The Iatan Generating Station has established operation, maintenance and inspection procedures for the anhydrous ammonia system. There are Operation and Maintenance manuals for each major piece of equipment, and personnel will receive training before being allowed to work on the systems. Ammonia sensors and alarms are in place to detect an ammonia release.  A fogging system to mitigate the impact of a release is in place. 

Management of Change [MOC] [40 CFR Part 68.75]
Written procedures are in place at Evergy to manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment, and procedures. Facility operators or any other employee whose job tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are promptly made aware of and offered training to deal with the modification(s).

Pre-Startup Safety Review [PSSR] [40 CFR Part 68.77]
Pre-start up safety reviews related to new processes and modifications to existing processes are conducted ro

utinely at Evergy. These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment, operating, and maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation.

Compliance Audits [40 CFR Part 68.79]
Evergy conducts audits on a regular basis to determine whether the provisions set out under the US EPA RMP and OSHA PSM regulations are being implemented. These audits are conducted at least every 3 years and any corrective actions required as a result of the audits are undertaken in a prompt manner.

Incident Investigation [40 CFR Part 68.81]
Evergy promptly investigates any incident that has resulted in or could reasonably result in a catastrophic release of a regulated substance. These investigations are undertaken to identify the situation leading to the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent the release from reoccurring. All reports are retained for a minimum period of 5 years.

Employee Participation [40 CFR Part 68.83]
Evergy believes that Process Safety Management and accident prevention is a team effort. Employees are strongly encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements. In addition, Evergy employees have access to all information created as part of the facility's implementation of the RMP and PSM rules, including information resulting from Process Hazard Analyses in particular.

Hot Work Permit [40 CFR Part 68.85]
Evergy has a hot work permit that requires issuance of a hot work permit for hot work operations conducted on or near the covered process.

Contractors [40 CFR Part 68.87] 
Evergy hires contractors to conduct specialty maintenance activities. Prior to selecting a contractor, a thorough evaluation of the contractor's safety performance is carried out. Evergy has a strict policy of informing the contractors of known potential hazards associated with the contractor's work and the corresponding processes. Contractors are also informed of all the

procedures for emergency response in the event of an accidental release of a regulated substance.

The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:

The Iatan Generating Station has had no accidental releases in the past five years which need to be reported in the five-year accident history.

The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:

In the event of an incident, Evergy Iatan has systems in place to respond quickly. Processes can be shut down on an emergency basis and the plant has a plan in place for evacuations, adequate first aid, and medical treatment and notification of local emergency response agencies. The facility is considered non- and relies on the Platte County Dispatch  to respond to chemical releases.

Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:

Evergy is committed to continually improve the RMP Program and safety systems. The Iatan Generating Station has an effort in place to improve the facilitys program documentation for the ammonia processes to ensure a successful program. This includes the completion of their most recent PHA, audit, and PSI review for an overall effective system.

Evergy has completed this report to provide the public with information about our activities at this facility.  We believe that, due to the many controls instituted to maintain a safe operation and our commitment to continuous improvement, an incident affecting our employees or the surrounding area is unlikely to occur.
